newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: PHILIPS Q1 UP AS CONSUMER UNIT RECOVERS.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPS Q1 UP AS CONSUMER UNIT RECOVERS.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV's first quarter 1997 net profit from normal operations rose 22 percent, boosted by a swing into profit by its consumer products unit, the company said on Wednesday.

Net profit from normal operations rose to 460 million guilders from 377 million, with the consumer products unit delivering a 206 million guilder operating profit, compared to a first quarter 1996 operating loss of 52 million.
Philips said in a statement the deconsolidation of its loss making Grundig affiliate and better operating performances in sound and vision and domestic appliances boosted the unit.

Philips said early this year it would no longer absorb all of the losses at German consumer electronics unit Grundig at the operating level. Instead it would become a passive minority shareholder, accounting for its 32 percent stake in its accounts under equity income of unconsolidated companies.

This item showed a 10 million guilder loss in the first quarter compared to an 84 million gain a year earlier, while group operating profit climbed to 836 million guilders from 690 million in the first quarter of 1996.
Grundig, which made a 1996 net loss of 553 million marks, has predicted sharply lower operating losses for 1997.
